To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the self assembly of a phospholiphid monolayer can be controlled by a semi fluorinated amphiphile to form a new kind of complex flower like patterns.
monolayers containing a mixture of DPPC and di( F 16 H 32) self assemble to flower like patterns that consist of a central core surrounded by a crown of smaller domains.
we found that monolayer of DPPC and semi fluorinated di( F 16 H 10) self assemble on the surface of the water and on solid substrate to form flower-like patterns that have hierarchical organization.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the self-assembly of amphiphilic molecules in monolayers at the air-water interface and in the bulk phase.
the self organization and the properties of complex nanostructured materials.
the self-assembly of phospholipid and semi fluorinated amphiphile monolayers on the surface of a liquid.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
these flower like patterns are a new class of self assembled nanostructures.

these flower like patterns are formed due to a combination of the intermolecular interaction between the hydrophobic chains of the phospholipids and the hydrophilic heads, as well as the interaction of the phospholippids with the solid substrate.

the formation of flower-like patterns is a result of the interplay of two main factors: (i) the self-assembly of DPPC into domains of different sizes and (ii) the self-organization of the semi fluorinated tecton into nanodomains.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we discovered an unusual self assembled structure that is formed when a fluorinated amphiphile is added to a monolayer of phospholipid.

the formation of the flower like patterns in monolayers is driven by a combination of the hydrophilic/hydrophobic interactions between the phospholipid and the semi fluorinated tethers and the hydrophobic/hydrophobic interaction between the phospholipo and the fluorocarbon tails.
the self assembly of the fluorocarbon chains of the tetrablock amphiphile leads to the formation of nanodomains that are responsible for the organization of the monolayer.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the self-assembly of DPPC with a small amount of semi fluorinated alkane leads to the formation of complex flower-like patterns.
the self assembly of DPPC and semi fluorinated di( F 16 H 16 ) leads to the formation of a complex hierarchical organization of the monolayers.
the self assembled nanodomans can impact the organization and phase behavior of a phospholiphid monolayer.
